content.overview: BNS s. 290 — Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings, etc. Read with the chapter heading and neighbouring sections. A BNS provision with no single IPC predecessor. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 290 is the rule on “Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings, etc”. The section provides that . Whoever, in pulling down, repairing or constructing any building, knowingly or negligently omits to take such measures with that building as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from the fall of that building, or of any part thereof, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 290 exists so that “Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.
